parsed.explanation: Federal law imposes up to 20 years plus mandatory whipping for same-sex conduct and applies to tourists; all states also criminalise Muslim cross-dressing enforced by religious departments, with documented raids, state-licensed targeting, a hunt for a trans woman, custody assaults and impunity after 2019 killings. Enforcement in private is uncommon and tourists are rarely targeted, and execution is not documented, which keeps the rating above 0.15-0.25. However active venue raids, delayed release despite a magistrate, no hate-crime or anti-discrimination recourse, and birth-sex custody risks make consequences after outing severe.

entry_documents.exposure: No explicit trans visa rule documented. Federal offences apply to tourists; foreign nationals were among 208 arrested in 2025 sauna raid and needed embassy intervention.
entry_documents.interaction: Document or presentation mismatch could lead to investigation under federal or, for Muslims, state religious offences.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented strip-search and sexual assault by religious officials, repeated arrests, prison terms of months to years with male-ward sexual violence, and delayed release after magistrate rejected remand.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Magistrate rejected one remand extension; legal aid mobilised bailors and embassies intervened for foreigners.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest for cross-dressing or same-sex conduct can become birth-sex custody, rehabilitation detention up to one year, and further outing.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: All 13 states bar Muslim men dressing as women, three also bar women posing as men, with no legal definition of transgender dressing; facilities by documents not documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Federal court struck down some state provisions on federalism grounds, without decriminalising federal conduct; court upheld cross-dressing ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State religious enforcement interacts with federal Penal Code, creating overlapping exposure in every state and federal territory.

care_services.exposure: Discriminatory denial of health care documented for trans people; medication confiscation or visitor care access not documented.
care_services.interaction: Discovery in care could trigger outing to staff, but dossier does not document a visitor-specific care pathway.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Minister gave religious department full licence for enforcement against trans people in 2020; 122 officers mobilised to hunt a trans woman in 2021; raids on queer venues in 2018, 2022, 2023, 2025.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Hate-speech content code covers sexual orientation; home affairs minister floated revisiting provisions in December 2025.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat-framing increases outing and raid risk; federalism rulings did not remove the underlying federal offences.

minors_guardians.exposure: No youth-specific health-care, medication or travel finding documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor would face the same document, raid and custody exposures as an adult if outed; no distinct rule documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Three trans women killed in under two months to June 2019 with police mistreatment and impunity documented; most recent documented killing is 2019, no later rate documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No hate-crime or anti-discrimination law documented; prosecution of attackers not documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Dated killings plus official targeting suggest low recourse, but current frequency cannot be inferred from 2019 alone.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination or hate-crime protection; conversion therapy promoted; rehabilitation retreats drew 1,733 attendees by 2021; remedies for visitors largely undocumented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts struck some state provisions and legal-aid groups mobilised in 2025; effects limited and did not decriminalise federal offences.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Paper litigation coexists with delayed release and impunity, indicating recourse is partial and slow rather than effective.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: birth-sex prison placement with assaults, cross-dressing offences, brief-to-years custody and no execution. This case is somewhat higher because private consensual enforcement is uncommon, tourists are rarely targeted, and Sharia cross-dressing applies only to Muslims, but longer federal penalties and active 2025 raids keep it near this tier.

Lower than 0.35: that anchor involves detention, fines and ineffective complaints but rarely imprisonment. Here imprisonment up to 20 years plus whipping, custody sexual violence, state hunt and documented killings with impunity are more severe, despite tourists rarely being targeted.

Higher than 0.15: that anchor has routine arrest for presentation, months of pretrial beatings and an unused capital provision. Here no execution pathway is documented, private enforcement is uncommon, magistrates and embassies provided some check in 2025, so lethal state custody is not established.

parsed.synthesis: The combined federal-state regime creates overlapping criminal exposure: federal same-sex offences apply to everyone, while state religious laws target Muslim gender nonconformity in every jurisdiction. Documented raids, official licensing of enforcement, outing via media leaks, birth-sex custody harms and absence of protective recourse mean discovery can lead to arrest, imprisonment, assault or forced rehabilitation. Mitigants are episodic enforcement, rare targeting of tourists in private, occasional judicial and legal-aid intervention, and no documented execution. Infrequent but severe state action places the traveller in the high-risk band, above routine-arrest lethal tiers but below exclusion-only regimes.
